header: THE SAMPLE QUESTIONS OF THE USER GUIDE: one data file, read by src/components/HelpManualModal.tsx. I write nothing about a question in the component, so a new area of the search (a new directory, a new tool) is one new entry here, not a change to the screen. Every question was taken from a question the project has already run or tested (the router and hospital tests, the employee-directory examples), and my one rule is that a question that names a PERSON is a template ("[name]"), never a real employee. src/lib/help/sampleQuestions.selftest.ts keeps the guide honest: no ordinary sample may be one the front gate sends to the deep search (synthesisIntent.ts), except those marked `either`. The deep search (EDS) has its own tab of the guide (src/lib/help/edsGuide.ts); I describe nothing about it on the sample questions page. THE ORDER IS THE ORDER OF THE BAR (23 Nov 2026): the sections follow the choices under the box (People, PAX, Hospital OPD, Holidays, Degrees, Circulars & Notices; Everything is the default and has no section of its own). Each section names its choice (`choice`) and says in one sentence which button to press and what that button does (`choose`). The sample selftest runs the PAX, Hospital OPD and Degrees questions through the real engines, with the choice's own line-making, so that a question shown under a button is one that button really answers. A "[bracket]" in a question is a blank to fill in: the guide shows it highlighted, and "Try it" puts the text in the search box for the reader to edit before pressing Enter.

doc: One short line: what the answer will be, or why the question is a good one.

members.name: instant
doc: The result appears as you type, with no Enter (a number, a site or department name); every other question needs Enter.

members.name: either
doc: Marks a question that may be sent to the deep search for a signed-in executive and to the ordinary search for everyone else (the front gate decides), so I do not test it as ordinary.

behaviours: the guide has many questions (more than 80) in at least nine sections
section ids are unique and every section says what it covers and how to ask
no question is written twice in one section
the recipe and the weak/good pairs exist
no ordinary sample is routed to the deep search
the sample page has no deep-search section, no ladders, no executives-only badge, and says nothing of EDS or Deep Synthesis
some questions are marked as appearing as you type (numbers, sites)
every instant sample really is one: an identifier the directory answers live, a site or department the site list finds, or a sum, conversion or date question the calculator answers
every sample marked 'press Enter' that is a calculator request opens a form, the menu or the page of all the services, and none of them is a live tool answer
no sample that needs Enter is an identifier (those appear on their own)
every area says how to run it, and says Enter or 'as you type'

the first tab's sections follow the buttons under the box (23 Nov 2026): people (two sections), PAX, hospital, holidays, degrees, then circulars & notices (three sections); none of them is the utility block
every section has a choice that begins with a button of the bar and a sentence saying which one to press; the buttons follow the bar's order
every button of the bar has a section in the guide
the department section is named for what it is (people by department and designation), and the utility block still carries the calculators, converters and live cards
a name search is a template
blanks are found and split
an empty search keeps every section
a word narrows to the questions that hold it, in their sections
all words must be present, and nothing found gives nothing
the two window events have distinct names the guide, the top bar and the search bar share
the guide reads its questions from the data file and has its four tabs (sample questions, Utility Services, how it works, deep search)
the top bar opens the guide on request and sends a question to the search bar
the search bar types a prefilled question into its box
the similar-sounding example names Goutam, Gautam and Gautham
every PAX sample is understood by the PAX engine under the PAX button
every Hospital OPD sample is answered by the hospital engine under the Hospital OPD button
every Degrees sample is answered by the table of degrees or the hospital's list of doctors' qualifications under the Degrees button (the PhD holders come from the directory, checked in the browser)
the Degrees section carries the bar's own examples
the Hospital OPD section carries the bar's own examples that are questions of a doctor and a day
